ghaffari-grunau-2024-network-decompositi.title: Near-Optimal Deterministic Network Decomposition and Ruling Set, and Improved MIS
ghaffari-grunau-2024-network-decompositi.verificationNote: The deterministic theorem includes degree+1 lists. The randomized corollary states ordinary Δ+1 coloring through CLP shattering; preserve that stated contract.

halldorsson-kuhn-nolin-tonoyan-2022-degr.title: Near-Optimal Distributed Degree+1 Coloring
halldorsson-kuhn-nolin-tonoyan-2022-degr.verificationNote: Theorem 1 colors a high-degree subset with local failure Δ^{-c}; setting the degree upper bound to n yields simultaneous high-degree coverage. Theorem 2 completes all vertices.

harris-schneider-su-2018-local-color.title: Distributed (Δ+1)-Coloring in Sublogarithmic Rounds
harris-schneider-su-2018-local-color.verificationNote: Randomized Δ+1-list coloring; retains the exact degree-dependent historical formula.

chang-li-pettie-2020-color.title: Distributed (Δ+1)-Coloring via Ultrafast Graph Shattering
chang-li-pettie-2020-color.verificationNote: Randomized Δ+1-list coloring reduces to deterministic degree+1-list coloring on polylogarithmic-size graphs. Keep Det_d symbolic rather than assigning an invented exponent.

ghaffari-kuhn-2021-deterministic.title: Deterministic Distributed Vertex Coloring: Simpler, Faster, and without Network Decomposition
ghaffari-kuhn-2021-deterministic.verificationNote: The LOCAL deterministic bound applies to degree+1 lists. The randomized corollary states ordinary Δ+1 coloring with global high probability.

halldorsson-nolin-tonoyan-2021-ultrafast.title: Ultrafast Distributed Coloring of High Degree Graphs
halldorsson-nolin-tonoyan-2021-ultrafast.verificationNote: Full Δ+1-list coloring requires maximum degree at least log^{2+δ}n for fixed δ>0. Theorem is stronger CONGEST. HKNT22 incorporates this report's LOCAL work; do not count it as an independent frontier.

flin-halldorsson-jakob-maus-2026-optimal.title: Sublogarithmic Distributed Vertex Coloring with Optimal Number of Colors
flin-halldorsson-jakob-maus-2026-optimal.verificationNote: Sufficiently large Δ; q≥Δ−k_Δ+1. Output is a valid q-coloring or a local non-colorability certificate. The exceptional Δ≥log^{50}n regime is faster. No imported boundary hardness.

linial-1992-locality.title: Locality in Distributed Graph Algorithms
linial-1992-locality.verificationNote: Three-coloring an n-cycle takes at least (log* n−3)/2 rounds. Use only the deterministic case here, even with a consistent orientation. No all-degree/palette lower projection.

flin-ghaffari-halldorsson-kuhn-nolin-202.title: A Distributed Palette Sparsification Theorem
flin-ghaffari-halldorsson-kuhn-nolin-202.verificationNote: Strict sampled-edge upper: Δ≥C log⁴n, O(log²Δ) rounds. The all-degree O(log²Δ+log³log n) implementation may retain original edges in its low-degree branch. The lower remains for sampled cliques with Bernoulli palette sampling and success 2/3, not ordinary LOCAL.

barenboim-elkin-kuhn-2014-linear-degree.title: Distributed (Δ+1)-Coloring in Linear (in Δ) Time
barenboim-elkin-kuhn-2014-linear-degree.verificationNote: Full journal theorem confirms O(Δ)+(1/2)log* n rounds for ordinary Δ+1 coloring. Specializing Δ=2 supplies the cycle upper in the reference inset.

fraigniaud-heinrich-kosowski-2016-confli.title: Local Conflict Coloring
fraigniaud-heinrich-kosowski-2016-confli.verificationNote: Set conflict degree d=1 in Theorem 4.1: lists of size degree(v)+1 suffice; exact bound is O(√Δ log^{5/2}Δ)+log* n.
